De Hayes, Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs Re: Interim Governance Date: October 28, 2020 Iam writing to designate you, as Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences, the interim authority responsible for the oversight of the Center for Peace and Nonviolence at The University of Rhode Island.
In that role, you will replace the Provost as the authority overseeing the Center.
In that role, please appoint an Interim Director and oversee the facuity senate process to formally transfer the responsibility for the Center from the Office of the Provost to the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.
In this designee role, you will have overall responsibility for the Center and its budgets.
The Interim Director, and ultimately the Director, will have responsibility for managing the operations, programs, and staff of the Center.
The Interim Director will report to you as the designated authority for the Center.

Center History and Purpose My understanding is that the Center for Nonviolence & Peace Studies was given permanent status as a "Center" in 2002 and has reported through the Provost Office since that time.
The Center continues to be an important component for study and activism at the University of Rhode Island.
Asyouknow,we have begun working through the faculty senate process to transfer the responsibility for and the location of the Center from the Provost Office to the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences.
In addition, our intention is to transfer the existing budget and also the course code relating to any existing or future courses offered by the Center.
However, until review and approval by the faculty senate has been completed, 1 ask that you serve as my designee responsible as the reporting authority for the Center and its Director.

Assuming positive action by fhe faculty senate at some future date, the Center will then be officially relocated within the College of Arts and Sciences, although faculty and student involvement should continue to span colleges and departments at the university in keeping with the decidedly interdisciplinary purpose of the Center articulated when it was established.
As articulated in the original Center proposal, which was supported by the College of Arts and Sciences Curriculum Committee, the Center is “an interdisciplinary partnership for research, teaching, and outreach related to nonviolence and peace studies as applied to individual and community development, conflict resolution and reconciliation, and constructive social change.
